docs.title: Dodge Durango R/T 2018: питание F85
docs.text: Диагностика одновременного и постоянного отказа нескольких систем на Dodge Durango R/T 2018 (5.7 HEMI, AWD, VIN 1C4SDJCT3JCXXXXXX).

docs.title: Статус на 8 ноября 2026
docs.text:
Найдено: реле K15 «Run 1» не включается — на его катушку (гнездо 85) не приходит управляющий сигнал

Питание реле и масса в норме, само реле исправно. Почему нет сигнала, пока не установлено. Возможны три причины:

  1. BCM не выдаёт сигнал на этот выход (неисправен выход или BCM отключил его сам, например после замыкания в цепи);
  2. оборван провод K619 между BCM и блоком PDC;
  3. обрыв внутри блока PDC между колодкой C7 и гнездом реле.

Оговорка: гнездо 85 мерили с вынутым реле. Без нагрузки BCM может не выдавать сигнал, поэтому следующие замеры — с реле на месте.

Что не работает: лампа SRS (подушки), Blind Spot Monitoring, задняя камера (синий экран), передний вентилятор салона, обогрев сидений и руля.

Почему всё сразу. Всё это питается от реле K15 «Run 1» в подкапотном блоке PDC:

  • F96, F97, F98 — обогрев и вентиляция сидений, обогрев руля;
  • F95 — радары BSM и задняя камера;
  • катушка реле K16 — передний вентилятор;
  • катушка реле K12 «Run 2» → F85 → модуль подушек (ORC).

Реле K15 включает блок BCM сигналом по проводу K619 (BCM C5, контакт 36 → колодка PDC C7, контакт 12 → гнездо 85 реле K15). На гнезде 85 этого сигнала нет, поэтому реле не включается.

BCM при этом в целом работает: он включает реле K08 «Run/Start» (F86 под напряжением) и реле дворников. Значит, зажигание он видит, и вопрос именно в выходе на K15 или в цепи после него.

docs.title: Следующий шаг: где теряется сигнал K619
docs.text:
Начинать можно с любого конца провода. Замер прямо на выходе BCM (шаг 2) сразу делит поиск пополам: 12 В у BCM — виноваты провод или PDC, 0 В — BCM или замыкание в цепи. Выбирайте то, до чего проще добраться.

Проверка выхода BCM: где блок, какой контакт, как мерить

  1. Колодка PDC C7, контакт 12 — реле K15 на месте, зажигание RUN, щуп на провод K619 (тонкий, коричневый с оранжевой полосой) со стороны проводов.
    • 12 В — BCM сигнал даёт, обрыв внутри блока PDC между колодкой и гнездом реле (клемма 12 или дорожка). Ремонт — замена PDC в сборе или ремонт клеммы.
    • 0 В — к шагу 2.
  2. BCM, колодка C5 (чёрная), контакт 36 — у правой кик-панели, тот же провод, реле на месте, RUN.
    • 12 В — BCM сигнал даёт, оборван провод K619 между BCM и PDC.
    • 0 В — BCM не выдаёт сигнал. Перед тем как винить BCM, проверьте провод на замыкание (шаг 3): BCM может сам отключить выход, если в цепи было замыкание на массу.
  3. Провод K619 без питания — зажигание OFF, реле K15 вынуто, колодка C5 отсоединена от BCM:
    • от контакта 36 колодки C5 до гнезда 85 реле K15 — меньше 3 Ом (провод цел);
    • от гнезда 85 до минуса АКБ — обрыв (OL). Низкое сопротивление — замыкание на массу: его нужно найти до любой замены BCM.
  4. Сканер: коды BCM (особенно B2121), ORC и BSM. Код подскажет, что BCM видит в цепи: обрыв или замыкание.

Безопасность

Никаких перемычек на F85 и на разъёмы подушек. Контрольную лампу к F85, F86 и разъёмам ORC не подключать. Реле и колодки вынимать только при выключенном зажигании.

docs.title: Question 1: Front blower power path. Which relay drives the motor, what feeds it, what energises the coil, and what roles do the power module and F99 play?
Takeaway
docs.text:
The front blower runs through PDC relay K16 "Blower Motor" (connector D876): - Terminal 30 is battery (B+, hot at all times). - Terminal 87 feeds F13 40A, then PDC C7-21 (circuit C7, DB), then the front blower power module. - The coil is energised by no module at all. Coil terminal 85 is fed directly from the output of the RUN 1 relay (K15). Coil terminal 86 is grounded through PDC C7-16 (circuit Z919) to G919A.

Blower speed is controlled separately: the A/C heater module (ATC) sends a PWM signal on C56 to power module C1-3. F99 is the A/C heater module's RUN/START ignition feed, not part of the motor's power path. K16 therefore closes whenever K15 RUN 1 is energised.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED. PDC relay designations: K16 = D876 "Blower Motor", K15 = D842A "Run 1", K12 = D842B "Run 2", K08 = D893 "Run / Start", K13 = D816 "Blower Motor - Rear", K06/K14 = Run/Accessory 1/2. Source: the PDC table image ("Dodge Durango (WD)", Underhood PDC). Run 1 relay location page — image GCWD1243624; PDC layout
  • VERIFIED (layout image). K12, K13, K14, K15 and K16 sit side by side in the front row of the PDC's lower relay field, at the "Front" edge. PDC layout page
  • VERIFIED. K16 Blower Motor Relay wiring:
  • 30 = "HOT AT ALL TIMES".
  • 87 → FUSE 13 40A → PDC C7 pin 21, DK BLU.
  • 86 → PDC C7 pin 16, BLK → S2505 → G919A. The diagram's location note for G919A is "behind front of right quarterpanel".
  • 85 ← a wire inside the PDC from the RUN 1 RELAY's 87 output.
  • Source: Automatic A/C Circuit 1/4, page, SVG VA585297
  • VERIFIED, cross-check from a second diagram. In Power Distribution Circuit 1/4, Blower Motor Relay terminal 85 ties into the RUN 1 relay output bus at the F98 node. That bus also feeds F95, F96, F97, F98 and the RUN 2 relay coil (85). Power Distribution page, SVG VA586498
  • VERIFIED. End view of K16 (D876): "Relay_Micro", harness family PDC_Underhood, pin 86 = Z919 internal GROUND. Relay-Blower Motor D876
  • VERIFIED. PDC C7 pinout (PDC C7 end view):
  • pin 21 = C7, DB, 4.0 mm², "BLOWER MOTOR SUPPLY"
  • pins 4, 16, 39 = Z919, BK, "GROUND"
  • pin 12 = K619, BN/OG, "IGNITION RUN CONTROL OUTPUT"
  • pin 13 = F923, PK/YE, "RUN RELAY CONTROL"
  • VERIFIED. Front blower path downstream of the PDC:
  • DK BLU circuit C7 → XY5020A pin 29 → front blower power module C1 pin 6 "BLOWER MTR SPLY".
  • Module C1-5 GND → BLK Z911 → G911A ("under front of center console").
  • Module C1-3 "BLOWER CTRL" ← DK BLU/BLU C56, from A/C heater module C1 pin 15.
  • Module C2-1 → DK BLU/WHT (C7) → blower motor pin 1 "BLOWER MTR SPLY".
  • Module C2-2 ↔ DK BLU/BRN Z134 ↔ blower motor pin 2 "BLOWER MTR CTRL". This pair is shielded, with an NCA drain (S000).
  • Source: Automatic A/C Circuit 2/4, SVG VA585298, on the A/C diagrams page
  • VERIFIED. End view of blower power module C1: 3 = C56 DB/BU "BLOWER CONTROL"; 5 = Z911 BK 4.0 "GROUND"; 6 = C7 DB 4.0 "BLOWER MOTOR SUPPLY". Module-Power-Blower Motor-Front C1
  • VERIFIED. The blower power module runs on PWM. The A/C-heater control's PWM signal goes to a comparator that compares it with blower motor feedback, and the module outputs a linear voltage that sets the speed. The module is diagnosed with a scan tool. Blower motor power module operation
  • VERIFIED. A/C heater module power and bus (VA585297):
  • C1-2 "FSD B(+)": RED A937 ← F49 10A (hot at all times) via PDC C5-25 / S2426.
  • C1-1 "FUSED IGN RUN/START CTRL OUTPUT": PNK/GRN F948, via S2449 / XY5020A-15 / S2448 ← PDC C6-36 ← F99 10A. Per Power Distribution 3/4 (VA586500) and Automatic A/C 3/4 (VA585299), F99 is "HOT W/ RUN/START RELAY ENERGIZED".
  • C1-6 ground: BLK Z912 → G912A.
  • C1-4 / C1-5: CAN IHS (+/−), circuits D101 / D102.
  • VERIFIED. PDC C6 pin 36 = F948, PK/GN, "FUSED IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT" (F99 output). PDC C6 end view
  • VERIFIED. Factory fuse table:
  • F13 40A "Blower Motor Front"
  • F49 10A "Integrated Central Stack/Climate Control"
  • F99 10A "Climate Control/Driver Assistance Systems Module/DSRC"
  • F37 25A "Rear Blower Motor"
  • F103 10A "Cabin Heater (Diesel)/Rear HVAC"
  • Sources: Fuse - Relay Locations And Types. The owner's manual has the same entries (2018 Durango OM PDF).
  • VERIFIED. The rear blower (for comparison) is a separate chain:
  • K13 Rear Blower Motor Relay: 30 = B+; 87 → F37 25A → PDC C7-3 (BLU/BRN C51) → rear blower power module pin 3.
  • K13 coil 85 ← PDC C7-8 ← external loop from C6-28 ← F103, which is on RUN 2.
  • K13 coil 86 → PDC C7-4 → G919A.
  • Source: VA585297, VA586498

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE. The front blower motor needs all of the following:
  • (a) K15 RUN 1 energised and its 87 output live (this energises the K16 coil);
  • (b) K16 contacts and F13;
  • (c) circuit C7 continuous through PDC C7-21 and XY5020A-29 to module C1-6;
  • (d) G911A ground at module C1-5;
  • (e) a PWM command from the A/C heater module on C56, which in turn needs F49 + F99 + CAN;
  • (f) a healthy module and motor.

The climate UI works and the speed bars change, which points to (e) being alive. A dead K15 output, a dead K16, or a break in the F13/C7 path would each leave the motor still. - STRONG INFERENCE. No module switches K16. It follows RUN 1. Checking 12 V at power module C1-6 (DB, circuit C7) with ignition RUN would show directly whether the power side is alive, which separates PDC-side faults from module/motor faults. - STRONG INFERENCE. K16, K15, K12 and K13 are all "Relay_Micro" parts. Their end-view pages share the same pin-face image (GCWD1006402), and their titles lack the "(On PCB)" tag given to the soldered relays (A/C clutch, fuel pump, horn, wipers). That suggests they are plug-in micro relays. There is a conflict, however: the PDC description says the PDC "houses the maxi-type cartridge fuses and solid state relays" (PDC description). Whether they are removable has to be confirmed visually.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The wiring diagram does not state the internal resistance of the K16/K15 coils or the K16 contact rating.
  • No 2018 Durango blower-specific TSB was found (see Q4).
  • The diagram's location text "G919A (behind front of right quarterpanel)" for a ground of the engine-compartment PDC relays could not be checked against a photo; location image GCWD1242919 was not reviewed.

docs.title: Question 2: BSM power. Fuse, relay and grounds for the left and right rear radar sensors, which CAN bus they use, and the master/slave arrangement
Takeaway
docs.text: Both blind-spot radars (LBSS and RBSS) share the same supply chain: - Source: F95 10A, "HOT W/ RUN 1 RELAY ENERGIZED" (K15). - Path: PDC C7-13 → circuit F923 PK/YE "RUN RELAY CONTROL" → splice S2442 (right front door sill, "W/ BLIND SPOT") → XY4000A-12 → I701-J → S04A (rear fascia harness) → pin 5 of each sensor. - Ground: circuit Z917 → S03A → I701-E → G917A (left front of cargo area). - Bus: both sit on CAN-IHS. The LBSS is the master and the RBSS the slave. The LBSS talks to the BCM (the CAN gateway), which relays to the cluster on CAN-C.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED. BSM circuit (Navigation Fig 1, VA584193 on the Navigation diagrams page):
  • Power: "HOT W/ RUN 1 RELAY ENERGIZED" FUSE 95 10A → C7-13 PNK/YEL → S2442 → XY4000A-12 → I701-J → S04A → LBSS pin 5 and RBSS pin 5, labelled "RUN RLY CTRL".
  • LBSS: pin 6 DK BLU/WHT CAN IHS(+); pin 7 WHT CAN IHS(−); pin 8 BLK GND.
  • RBSS: pins 8 and 3 BLK GND; pin 6 DK GRN/WHT CAN IHS(+); pin 7 WHT CAN IHS(−).
  • Grounds: → S03A → I701-E → G917A "(left front of cargo area)".
  • Mirror indicators: driven by the door modules (DDM C1-3 / C1-2, PDM C1-3 / C1-2).
  • VERIFIED. LBSS end view (harness Fascia_Rear): 5 = F923 PK/YE "RUN RELAY CONTROL"; 6 = D215 DB/WH CAN IHS(+); 7 = D216 WH CAN IHS(−); 8 = Z917 BK GROUND. Sensor-Blind Spot-Left D2481A
  • VERIFIED. RBSS end view: 3 = Z917 BK GND; 5 = F923 PK/YE; 6 = D217 DG/WH CAN IHS(+); 7 = D218 WH CAN IHS(−); 8 = Z917 BK GND. Sensor-Blind Spot-Right Rear D2480A
  • VERIFIED. Splice S2442 (Body harness) carries circuit F923 PK/YE 0.35 "RUN RELAY CONTROL". S2442 end view. G917A is circuit Z917 in the Under_Body harness (G917A).
  • VERIFIED. Bus roles: "The LBSS is a master node, while the RBSS is a slave node. The two nodes communicate with each other over the … CAN-IHS data bus." The LBSS reports to the BCM, and "the BCM, which is a CAN-C gateway, relays the message to the IC over the CAN-C data bus". The LBSS also messages the DDM/PDM (mirror icons) and the radio (chimes). Sensor, Blind Spot: Operation; BSM System Description
  • VERIFIED. The cluster message "SERVICE BLIND SPOT SYSTEM" means the BSM system is unavailable due to a monitored system fault. "TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE" means blockage or misalignment. D&T - Blind Spot Monitor System
  • VERIFIED. The LBSS DTC list includes B2199-16 (battery voltage below threshold), U0011-00 (CAN interior bus off), U0140-00 (lost communication with BCM), U0203/U0204 (lost communication with left/right door module) and U11FA-00 (lost communication with right blind spot sensor). LBSS Electrical Diagnostics
  • VERIFIED. Power Distribution 1/4 confirms F95 → C7-13 → S2442 "(right front door sill)(w/ blind spot)", and that F95 hangs off the RUN 1 relay's 87 bus. VA586498

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE. If both sensors lose F923, the master LBSS is silent on CAN-IHS. The BCM/cluster would then show the BSM fault ("SERVICE BLIND SPOT SYSTEM" or similar), and other modules would log lost-communication codes with the LBSS. No sensor DTCs can be read while the sensors are unpowered.
  • STRONG INFERENCE. Both sensors share one supply (F95 → C7-13 → S2442 → XY4000A → I701 → S04A) and one ground chain (S03A → I701-E → G917A). A simultaneous failure of both points upstream of S04A, or to a shared ground, rather than to the two sensors themselves.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• I did not find the exact cluster text this vehicle shows, nor a CAN-IHS U-code for the BCM losing the LBSS (the BCM DTC lists were not opened).
  • The sensors' current draw and whether they sleep on CAN were not found.

docs.title: Question 3: Rear camera. Power source, video receiver, and what causes the blue screen
Takeaway
docs.text:
The rear camera has no fuse of its own: - Power: circuit F923 from the same F95 / C7-13 / S2442 feed as the BSM ("RUN RLY CTRL"), then XY2120A-6 → I6742A-1 → camera. - Ground: Z923 → G923A (base of left D-pillar). - Wake-up: the BCM sends the imager wake-up over LIN (CBC 3, circuit D403, BCM C5-45) in reverse. - Video: analog NTSC on X970 / X971 / X972 (signal / return / shield) to radio C1 pins 31 / 32 / 33.

It does not go through the ParkSense module. The radio switching to the camera view proves that the reverse message is getting through. An empty or blue screen means no video arrives, and loss of the F923 run-relay feed is the first item in the factory list of possible causes.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED. Rear View Camera circuit (Navigation Fig 8, VA584199, Navigation diagrams page):
  • Power: "HOT W/ RUN 1 RELAY ENERGIZED" FUSE 95 10A → C7-13 PNK/YEL → S2442 "(W/ BLIND SPOT)" → XY2120A-6 → I6742A-1 → RED F923 → camera "RUN RLY CTRL".
  • Ground: camera GND BLK Z923 → I6742A-6 → XY2110A-14 → G923A ("base of left D pillar").
  • LIN: camera LIN BUS CBC 3 BLU D403 → I6742A-5 → XY2120A-10 → S2433 (right front door sill) → BCM C5-45 (ORG/DK BLU D403).
  • Video: CAMERA SIG X970 / RTN X971 / SHLD X972 → I6742A → XY2110A → XY5010A → Radio C1 pins 31 (SIG), 32 (RTN), 33 (SHLD).
  • VERIFIED. Radio side: premium radio C1-31 X970 "CAMERA SIG", C1-32 X971 "CAMERA RTN", C1-33 X972 "CAMERA SHIELD" (Radio diagrams; e.g. VA584344).
  • VERIFIED, with a conflict. The camera end view (harness Rear_Camera_Jumper, D6742A) lists 1 = F923 RD "RUN RELAY CONTROL", 2 = X970 GN, 3 = X971 WH, 4 = X972 shield, 5 = D403 BL LIN, 6 = Z923 BK GND (Camera-Rear end view). The wiring diagram VA584199 instead numbers the camera pins 1 = GND, 2 = LIN, 3 = RUN RLY CTRL, 4 = SHLD, 5 = RTN, 6 = SIG. Circuit codes and colours agree between the two; pin numbers at the camera are UNVERIFIED. Identify wires by circuit/colour, not by pin number.
  • VERIFIED. "The Rear View Camera (RVC) receives power from a run relay control output circuit located in the Power Distribution Center (PDC)… When the transmission is shifted into the Reverse position, the BCM sends a signal over the LIN bus to the RVC that excites the imager." Video is NTSC-M composite. The shield is grounded only at the radio. Camera, Rear: Operation
  • VERIFIED. "Rear Camera Inoperative With RRM Display":
  • Theory: "The fused ignition circuit supplies power to the camera… in reverse, the rear camera has priority."
  • Set condition: "No rear picture is displayed on Radio with the vehicle in reverse."
  • Possible causes (in order): FUSED RUN RELAY OUTPUT CIRCUIT, GROUND CIRCUIT, CAMERA SIGNAL, RETURN, SHIELD, camera.
  • Step 2: with the camera unplugged and ignition ON, measure F923 to ground for battery voltage. Step 3: Z923 ground below 5 Ω.
  • Sources: Theory, Possible Causes, Diagnostic Test
  • VERIFIED. The general rear-camera D&T table separates two cases. "No camera image… and no backup lamps" points to BCM inputs and outputs and the reverse input. "No camera image… backup lamps do operate" points to the camera ground, feed, shield, return and signal, or the camera itself. D&T - Rear Camera
  • VERIFIED, with a discrepancy. The fuse table and owner's manual label F95 "Rear Camera/ParkSense" (fuse spec; owner's manual). In the wiring diagram, however, the Park Assist Module is fed from F99 ("HOT W/ RUN/START RELAY ENERGIZED", C6-36 → S2448 → PAM C1-1), with ground C1-7 → G924A and CAN-C on C1-6 / C1-12 (Parking Assistant Circuit VA584200; Power Distribution 3/4 VA586500).

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE. The radio clearly receives the reverse status: it switches to the camera page. So the CAN reverse message and the radio's video input mode are working. The empty screen is consistent with no NTSC signal from the camera. The most likely cause is the missing F923 feed, because the BSM shares the same feed and is also dead.
  • UNVERIFIED. The service information does not say what colour the Uconnect screen shows when there is no video sync. The "blue screen" interpretation comes from general experience, not from the manual.
  • STRONG INFERENCE. If ParkSense (F99, RUN/START) still works while the camera does not, that supports a fault on the RUN 1 / F95 side rather than in RUN/START.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Camera current draw and the LIN message content are not documented.
  • The camera connector pin-number conflict (end view vs diagram) is unresolved.
  • I found no 2018 Durango TSB on a camera with no image apart from the radio-software "Radio and Back-up Camera Enhancements" bulletins 08-084-19 and 08-017-21 (titles only, from the carcomplaints list; not opened).

docs.title: Question 4: Do the BSM, camera or blower share a relay or fuse with F85? Concrete list of fuses and circuits
Takeaway
docs.text:
Yes. All three failed systems and F85 hang off the RUN 1 relay (K15): - BSM and camera: F95, which is on RUN 1's 87 bus. - Front blower: K16's coil, which is fed from RUN 1's 87 bus. - F85 (ORC): on the RUN 2 relay (K12) output, and the K12 coil is itself powered from RUN 1's 87 bus.

So one loss of K15's output kills all four symptoms at once. F86, the other ORC fuse, and F99 (HVAC/ParkSense) are on the separate RUN/START relay (K08), which matches F86 being normal and the engine and HVAC UI working.

The one item that does not fit is the reported "F95 normal" reading. If F95 really has 12 V under load with ignition RUN, K15 is working. In that case the four symptoms would need at least two separate faults: (a) C7-13/F923/S2442 for BSM + camera, and (b) the K12 RUN 2 relay for F85, plus a separate blower fault. F95 should be re-measured.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED. Power Distribution 1/4 (VA586498, page). I checked the crops at high resolution.
  • RUN 1 relay (K15): 30 = PDC internal B+ bus; 85 = PDC C7-12 BRN/ORG → BCM C5-36; 86 = internal ground bus → PDC C1-12 BLK → S2547 → G909A (right rear of engine compartment). Its 87 output bus feeds:
    • F95 10A → C7-13
    • F96 10A → C7-15
    • F98 20A → C7-19
    • F97 20A → C7-17
    • the Blower Motor Relay (K16) coil 85
    • the RUN 2 relay (K12) coil 85
  • RUN 2 relay (K12): 30 = B+; 85 ← RUN 1 output; 86 → the same ground bus. Its 87 output is a separate bus feeding:
    • F40 10A → C1-10
    • F103 10A → C6-28
    • F85 10A → C6-15
    • F101 15A → C6-32
    • F100 10A → C6-34
  • The RUN 1 bus ends at the F97 / RUN 2 coil node. It is not connected to the RUN 2 output bus.
  • VERIFIED. The SRS diagram confirms:
  • "HOT W/ RUN 2 RELAY ENERGIZED" FUSE 85 10A → PDC C6-15 PNK/YEL F929 → ORC C2-104 "FUSED IGN SW OUTPUT (RUN)".
  • "HOT W/ RUN/START RELAY ENERGIZED" FUSE 86 10A → PDC C6-13 PNK/GRN F945 → ORC C2-103 "IGN RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT".
  • ORC ground C2-101 BLK Z913 → G913A; ORC on CAN-C (C2-54 / C2-53).
  • Source: Supplemental Restraints 1/3 VA582314 (page)
  • VERIFIED. PDC C6 end view: 15 = F929 PK/YE "FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN)"; 13 = F945 PK/GN "IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT"; 10 = K617 BN "RUN/START RELAY CONTROL"; 28 = F931; 32 = F925; 34 = F938; 36 = F948. PDC C6
  • VERIFIED. Relay end views:
  • K15 Run 1 (D842A): 85 = K619 "IGNITION RUN CONTROL OUTPUT", 86 = Z909 GROUND. Run 1
  • K12 Run 2 (D842B): 86 = Z909 GROUND. Run 2
  • K08 Run/Start (D893): 30 = A0 B(+), 85 = Z909 GROUND, 86 = K617 control. Run/Start
  • Note: the diagram draws the Run/Start coil with 85 = control, while the end view gives 85 = ground. This is a minor pin-label discrepancy.
  • VERIFIED. Power Distribution 3/4 (VA586500): RUN/START relay coil ← PDC C6-10 BRN → BCM C1-18; 30 ← "FROM FUSE 25"; output bus feeds F77, F86, F99, F75, the vacuum-pump relay coil, and further fuses including F78, F76 and F88. Loads on this bus include the ORC (F86 → C2-103), park assist, A/C heater module, FFCM, rear A/C control, ACC, PCM, EPS, ABS, SGW and cluster.
  • VERIFIED. Factory fuse descriptions for the RUN 1 and RUN 2 buses (fuse spec):
  • F95 10A Rear Camera/ParkSense
  • F96 10A Rear Seat Heater Switch/Flashlamp Charger
  • F97 20A Rear Heated Seats & Heated Steering Wheel
  • F98 20A Ventilated Seats/Front Heated Seats
  • F40 10A Daytime Running Lights/Headlamp Leveling
  • F85 10A Airbag Module
  • F86 10A Airbag Module
  • F100 10A Active Damping
  • F101 15A Electrochromatic Mirror/Smart High Beams
  • F103 10A Rear HVAC
  • F99 10A Climate Control/DASM/DSRC
  • VERIFIED. Downstream loads per VA586498:
  • F96 → S02A F928 → rear heated-seat switches
  • F98 → S2441 / SF921A → seat vent motors / heated seats module C1-5
  • F97 → SF922A → heated seats module C3-6 / C4-2
  • F40 → S2526 → right front lamp assembly and headlamp leveling motors (premium)
  • F101 → XY5020A-7 → S2443 → in-car temperature sensor pin 3 and humidity sensor pin 3
  • F100 → SP2589 → active damping module C2-14 / C2-47
  • F103 → rear blower relay (K13) coil
  • VERIFIED. FCA GPOP tech tip 9003816 (11/01/2017, MY18 WD), PDC part numbers 68320920A / 68320923A: "For 2018 WD, prior to replacing the Power Distribution Center (PDC), you MUST contact the STAR Center … for diagnostic assistance and pre-authorization." It contains no symptom description. NHTSA PDF MC-10216108-9999; carcomplaints listing
  • Field reports, weak quality and UNVERIFIED for this VIN. A WebSearch summary of owner posts mentions a CarGurus thread (blind spot, then airbag light, then backup camera failing) and a Ram EcoDiesel thread (airbag light plus A/C fan not working, fixed at the airbag fuses). I could not open the CarGurus page (HTTP 406); the Ram thread is a different platform. CarGurus thread; ecodieselram

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE. All four failures (BSM, SRS warning, front blower, camera) are explained by one point: no output from RUN 1 relay K15. Candidate causes:
  • the relay itself;
  • its BCM drive, K619 BRN/ORG from BCM C5-36 to PDC C7-12;
  • its coil ground Z909 → PDC C1-12 → G909A, which is shared with K08/K12 (and since K08 works, that ground is probably fine);
  • its B+ feed;
  • the PDC-internal 87 bus.

With K15 off: F95 is dead (BSM + camera), K16 is not energised (front blower), and K12 is not energised, so F85 is dead (ORC C2-104 loses its RUN input and the SRS lamp comes on). F86 and F99 survive on K08. - STRONG INFERENCE. If K15 is the cause, these should also be dead (check them to confirm): - F96 (rear heated-seat switches) - F97 (rear heated seats, heated steering wheel) - F98 (front heated/ventilated seats) - F40 (DRL / headlamp leveling) - F101 (auto-dim mirror / smart high beams, plus the ATC humidity and in-car temperature sensors) - F103 (rear blower relay coil → rear blower) - F100 (active damping, if equipped)

These should still work because they are on Run/Start or Run/Acc: engine, ParkSense (F99), ABS/EPS, cluster, windows (Run/Acc 1 F66 / CB1), power outlets. - STRONG INFERENCE. How to read F95 and the other fuses: - F95 live but F85 dead, with K15 good: K12 RUN 2 (or its output) is failing, but RUN 2 cannot explain the BSM, camera or front blower. Those would need F923/S2442 (BSM + camera) and K16/F13/C7 (blower) faults as well. - F96/F97/F98 also dead: K15 is the culprit, and the F95 reading should be re-checked with a test light (loaded) on both fuse test points, ignition RUN. - Direct check: about 12 V on K15's coil control (PDC C7-12, BN/OG, from BCM C5-36) in RUN, and on the K15 87 bus. - STRONG INFERENCE (practical, needs confirmation that the relays plug in). K12–K16 are the same "Relay_Micro" type in one row. If they are removable, a known-good relay from a less critical position, e.g. K13 Rear Blower, could be swapped into K15 as a test. The PDC description's "solid state relays" wording conflicts with this; inspect visually first. - Shared splice: S2442 (right front door sill) and connector C7-13 are common only to the BSM and the camera, not to the blower or F85. A fault there could explain only the BSM + camera pair.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• I did not find how the BCM decides to drive K15 (K619), e.g. ignition RUN with engine running versus RUN only, or any BCM DTC for a K619 output fault. The BCM DTC pages were not opened.
  • No 2018 Durango TSB or recall specifically about RUN 1/RUN 2 relay or PDC failure symptoms was found. Tech tip 9003816 only requires STAR pre-authorization before PDC replacement.
  • Whether the K12/K15/K16 relays are removable or soldered could not be confirmed visually (see the Q1 conflict).
  • Inaccessible sources:
  • lemon-manuals "Repair and Diagnosis (Single Page)" returned a 21 GB null-byte tarpit when requested without an Accept header (split-tree pages worked with "Accept: text/html").
  • .../Electrical/Fuses & Circuit Breakers/ returned HTTP 404.
  • The cargurus.ca thread returned HTTP 406.
  • The second half of the carcomplaints 2018 Durango TSB list was not read.
  • Full log: docs/sources/blower-bsm-camera/_INDEX_and_inaccessible_log.md.
  • Adjacent-year and WK2 Grand Cherokee sources were not needed; every claim above comes from 2018 Durango documents.

docs.title: Q1. Which modules are on CAN-C and which on CAN-IHS (and on any private buses)? Covers ORC, BSM, HVAC, radio, ParkSense, camera, IPC, BCM, RF Hub, PCM.
Takeaway
docs.text:
The 2018 Durango has two CAN-C star connectors and two CAN-IHS star connectors, each pair joined by a trunk: - CAN-C: "Dash" star and "IP" star, joined by D64/D65. - CAN-IHS: "IP" star and "Body" star, joined by D145/D146.

The modules that matter here are on different buses and different stars: - ORC: CAN-C (IP star). - BSM radars: CAN-IHS (Body star). - A/C heater (HVAC) module: CAN-IHS (IP star). - Park Assist module: CAN-C (Dash star). - Radio: not on either star. It has point-to-point "A/T" CAN-C and CAN-IHS links to the Security Gateway. - Rear camera: no CAN pins at all. Its only network wire is BCM LIN "CBC 3".

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• Bus speeds are VERIFIED: CAN C runs at 500 kbps and CAN IHS (Interior High Speed) at 125 kbps — SM-CommOp
  • The "Communication – Operation" page has no list of which module is on which bus (VERIFIED absence). The module lists below come from the "Computer Data Lines" wiring diagram, 5 sheets — CDL page

STAR CAN C IP CONNECTOR (sheet 3; star ground Z912 → G912A "under center console"). STRONG INFERENCE except the module labels, which the diagram prints — CDL-3: - C1: D65 WHT/GRN, D64 WHT/BLU, Z912. Trunk to the Dash star. - C2: ORC. D11 YEL/DK BLU and D12 YEL → in-line XY5020A pins 11/12 → ORC C2 pin 54 "CAN C (+)" and pin 53 "CAN C (−)". Radio (Uconnect) is not on any star. STRONG INFERENCE — CDL-1: - Radio C1 pin 1 (GRY) is "CAN C (+) AT" and pin 11 (YEL) is "CAN C (−) AT". They go to Security Gateway C1 pin 4 (D436) and pin 11 (D435). - Radio C1 pin 2 (DK BLU) is "CAN IHS (+) AT" and pin 12 (WHT) is "CAN IHS (−) AT". Its only network wire is "LIN BUS CBC 3" (D403 ORG/DK BLU). That LIN runs from the BCM through XY2120A and splice S2433 (right front door sill) and is shared with the steering column control module. The trunk from IHS-IP star C1 appears to enter the BCM on one connector and leave on another towards IHS-Body star C1; - LIN BUS CBC 3 (D403), LIN BUS CBC 2 (D402: rain/light sensor, mirror, humidity sensor) and LIN BUS 1 (D401: intelligent battery sensor). - Other non-star links (STRONG INFERENCE) — CDL-3, CDL-4: - The keyless ignition node talks to the RF Hub over a "SECURITY K LINE COMM" (D122). - The forward-facing camera has a second pair (pins 7/8, TAN and WHT/TAN, D448/D449) running directly to the ACC module, not through a star. The diagram labels it "CAN C".

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• ORC (CAN-C, IP star C2) and the BSM sensors (CAN-IHS, Body star C4/C5) share no bus segment. The A/C heater module is on a third star (IHS-IP C3). The blower and the camera are not CAN loads at all.
  • A single CAN fault therefore cannot take out exactly these four functions while sparing the modules that share their stars:
  • the IPC, RF Hub and steering column module (IP star, with ORC);
  • the door modules (IHS-IP star, with the A/C heater module);
  • the liftgate and seat modules (IHS-Body star, with the BSM sensors).
  • The radio shows the camera screen on reverse. Reverse status comes from the shift-by-wire/TCM side on CAN-C and reaches the radio through the SGW "A/T" link. So the path CAN-C → SGW → radio is working.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• End views for the branch plugs C2–C13 were not fetched. Their pin numbers are inferred from the diagram, and pin 1 = (+) is assumed by analogy with the C1 end views. The CAN C IP C1 end view (D2599A) was also not fetched.
  • BCM pin numbers for its CAN and LIN connections were not in the extracted text.
  • The rear camera's power and video circuits are on the Radio/Navigation diagrams, which were not fetched.
  • Whether this R/T actually has each optional module (ACC, active damping, video) depends on the build, not on the diagram.

docs.title: Q2. Does the BCM act as the gateway? Does the 2018 Durango (VIN digit 10 = J) have a Security Gateway (SGW)?
Takeaway
docs.text: Both are true: - The BCM is the central gateway between CAN-C and CAN-IHS. - A Security Gateway Module (SGW, also written SGM) is part of the 2018 Durango service information and wiring. It sits between the diagnostic port (DLC) and Uconnect radio on one side and the internal CAN-C and CAN-IHS on the other.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED quote: the architecture "allows the Body Control Module (BCM) to be a Central Gateway to process and transfer messages" between CAN C and CAN IHS. Another VERIFIED quote: "These networks and their subnetworks are protected by a Security Gateway Module (SGM)." — SM-CommOp
  • VERIFIED: the 2018 Durango manual has a separate SGW DTC list (all three were read):
  • B2199-14/-16/-17 battery voltage;
  • B22A9-49 internal failure;
  • B235A-00 in-plant mode;
  • C221C-00 flash required;
  • U0001-00 CAN C BUS;
  • U0002-00 CAN C BUS OFF PERFORMANCE;
  • U0011-00 CAN INTERIOR BUS OFF PERFORMANCE.

Sources: SGW DTC index, SGW Electrical Diagnostics - VERIFIED: the manual also has an SGW removal procedure and SGW connector end views C1 (D3921A) and C2 (D3921B). Neither was fetched — SGW U0011 test (links), StarList - SGW wiring on data-lines sheet 1. The diagram shows no "with SGW" option note. Location text: "RIGHT CENTER OF DASH". STRONG INFERENCE pin map — CDL-1: - SGW C1: - pin 3 D428 TAN "DIA CAN C (+)" - pin 4 D436 "CAN C (+) AT" (to radio) - pin 5 D351 "CAN C (+)" (to CAN-C IP star C6) - pin 6 Z912 GND - pin 7 F949 "FSD IGN RUN/START" - pin 10 D427 YEL "DIA CAN C (−)" - pin 11 D435 "CAN C (−) AT" - pin 12 D350 "CAN C (−)" - SGW C2: - pin 1 D437 "CAN IHS (+) AT" - pin 2 D434 "DIA CAN IHS (+)" - pin 3 D353 "CAN IHS (+)" (to IHS-IP star C6) - pin 4 Z912 - pin 5 A902 "FSD B(+)" - pin 6 D438 "CAN IHS (−) AT" - pin 7 D433 "DIA CAN IHS (−)" - pin 8 D352 "CAN IHS (−)" - DLC ("UNDER LEFT END OF DASH"): - pins 6/14 = D428/D427 (diagnostic CAN C, to the SGW only); - pins 3/11 = D434/D433 (diagnostic CAN IHS, to the SGW only); - pins 4/5 = Z911 (ground G911A); - pin 16 = A900 B+. - SGW supply: - PDC Fuse 44 (10 A) and Fuse 45 (5 A), "hot at all times", feed DLC pin 16 and SGW B+. Which fuse feeds which was not resolved. - Fuse 88 (15 A), "hot w/ run/start relay energized", feeds splice S2450 and then SGW F949. - Trade press on fleet rollout (not Durango-specific): - Mopar's media manager said the SGW "was placed on most 2018 model year and newer FCA vehicles". The same article quotes CIC's Rozint saying RAM and Jeep Grand Cherokee received SGWs in 2019 — Repairer Driven News, 2020-01-20 - IOSiX said FCA put the SGW in "roughly half of their 2018 product line and nearly 90 percent of their 2019 vehicles" — VehicleServicePros, 2018-10-09 - Aftermarket bypass sellers list the 2018–2023 Durango as SGW-equipped. These are commercial sources — garageandfab, buyp3 - What the SGW blocks: the FCA overview says the SGW "does not restrict access to diagnostic data". Clearing DTCs and bi-directional tests need an authenticated tool (AutoAuth) — Repairer Driven News

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• Three different gateway behaviours follow from this layout:
  • The DLC and the radio talk to the vehicle only through the SGW, over separate "DIA" and "A/T" links.
  • The SGW itself is an ordinary node on CAN-C (IP star C6) and on CAN-IHS (IHS-IP star C6).
  • The BCM bridges messages between CAN-C (Dash star C7) and CAN-IHS (trunk D145/D146).
  • What an SGW failure would look like: the scan tool would see nothing on either bus, and the radio would lose all vehicle data, including reverse status and HVAC status. The user's radio still detects reverse, so the SGW and its F949 ignition feed are alive. STRONG INFERENCE.
  • Workshop practice: an aftermarket scan tool will read codes but needs AutoAuth (or a 12+8 bypass harness) to clear them. This matters when clearing ORC or BSM codes after the repair.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The service-information text gives no physical SGW location beyond the diagram note "right center of dash". The removal procedure was not read.
  • I did not find an FCA document that ties SGW fitment to a production date or VIN range for the Durango. The evidence is the 2018 WD service information plus vendor lists.

docs.title: Q3. Where are the CAN star connectors, what are their pinouts, and how does a technician isolate a branch (resistance, voltage)?
Takeaway
docs.text:
• Construction: each "star" is a housing that takes separate small plugs, one per branch (C1…C13). C1 is the 3-pin trunk: CAN(+), CAN(−) and a ground. Every other plug is a 2-pin module branch.
  • Termination: the termination resistors are inside the star connectors. Total bus resistance is about 60 Ω with the battery disconnected.
  • Isolation: unplug one branch plug at the star to separate that module and its wiring from the bus.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED: "Termination resistors are built into the Star Connectors." Total network resistance is about 60 Ω, measured with the battery disconnected. The bus is a twisted pair with 33–50 twists per metre — SM-CommOp
  • VERIFIED voltage table (DVOM between node ground and the CAN terminal; the meter shows an average) — SM-CommOp:
Condition CAN-L CAN-H Asleep / key off 0 V 0 V CAN-C recessive (idle) 2.4–2.5 V 2.4–2.5 V Active (dominant / key on) 1.3–2.3 V 2.6–3.5 V Short to ground ≈0 V ≈0 V (0.02 V) Short to battery battery voltage battery voltage − 0.75 V CAN-H shorted to CAN-L 2.45 V 2.45 V
  • Star connector C1 end views (VERIFIED, from OEM connector pages):
  • D2600A, STAR CAN C DASH C1 (natural colour, female, part 2-2138651-1): pin 1 D65 WH/GN CAN C (+); pin 2 D64 WH/BU CAN C (−); pin 3 Z909 BK ground — D2600A
  • D2601A, STAR CAN IHS IP C1 (GREEN, female, part 5-2138651-1): pin 1 D145 WH/GN CAN IHS (+); pin 2 D146 WH CAN IHS (−); pin 3 Z912 BK ground — D2601A
  • D2602A, STAR CAN IHS BODY C1 (natural colour, part 7283-8349): pin 1 D145 WH/GN CAN IHS (+); pin 2 D146 WH CAN IHS (−) — D2602A
  • VERIFIED: complete list of star plugs in the OEM connector index — StarList:
  • CAN C Dash: C1, C2, C3, C5–C12 (D2600A–M)
  • CAN C IP: C1–C7, C10, C12 (D2599A–L)
  • CAN IHS IP: C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7, C10–C13 (D2601A–M)
  • CAN IHS Body: C1–C6, C11, C12 (D2602A–L)
  • Branch plugs for the modules in question (STRONG INFERENCE, see Q1). Plug pin 1 = (+), pin 2 = (−):
  • ORC = CAN-C IP star C2 (D11/D12)
  • IPC = CAN-C IP C5 (D81/D82)
  • RF Hub = CAN-C IP C12 (D39/D40)
  • SGW = CAN-C IP C6 and IHS-IP C6
  • BCM = CAN-C Dash C7 (D45/D46)
  • PCM = CAN-C Dash C2
  • Park Assist = CAN-C Dash C8 (D77/D78)
  • A/C heater = IHS-IP C3 (D101/D102)
  • Left BSM = IHS-Body C4 (D215/D216)
  • Right BSM = IHS-Body C5 (D217/D218)

Sources: CDL-2, CDL-3, CDL-4, CDL-5 - Locations. VERIFIED that the figures exist; where each figure points is my visual reading, so STRONG INFERENCE: - The OEM location figure for D2601A (IHS-IP) is the "Instrument Panel Harness" view. Its pointer goes to the left (driver) end of the IP harness, left of the steering column — GCWD1243525 (saved). - The figure for D2600A (CAN-C Dash) is the "Headlamp & Dash Harness" view. Its pointer goes to the harness trunk along the cowl/dash panel on the engine-compartment side — GCWD1243641 (saved). - The figure for D2602A (IHS-Body) is the "Body Harness" view. Its pointer goes to a connector cluster in the mid-cabin floor / B-pillar area; which side could not be determined from the 3-D image — GCWD1243239 (saved). - The CAN-C IP star figure was not fetched. - The diagram's location notes refer to the star grounds, not the stars: G912A "under center console" (IP stars), G909A "right rear of engine compt" (Dash star), G923A "base of left D pillar" (Body star). - VERIFIED procedure from "No Response From ECU" (paraphrased) — No Response From ECU – Diagnostic Test: 1. Check the scan-tool topology ("Vehicle View"). 2. Load-test the fused B+ and ignition supplies with a 3156 bulb (about 2 A). Check the fuse first; if it is open, look for a short to ground. The procedure warns: "Do not load test air bag/restraint circuits." 3. Load-test the grounds. 4. Measure CAN (+) at the ECU connector. Below 2.6 V means an open or high resistance in CAN (+). 5. Measure CAN (−). Below 1.3 V means an open in CAN (−). 6. Inspect the connectors, then replace the ECU if it is still inactive. - VERIFIED: the SGW U0001/U0011 tests say to "use the wiring diagrams and CAN C/IHS star connectors to isolate opens, shorts, or a faulty module". The "Scan Tool Will Not Communicate With CAN Bus" procedure "diagnoses CAN Bus circuits after the Security Gateway". It also warns that U-codes may not appear until the fault is repaired — SGW U0011 test, Scan Tool Will Not Communicate With CAN Bus

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• Isolation method (standard star-topology practice, consistent with the OEM facts above):
  • Disconnect the battery and measure across CAN(+) and CAN(−) at any branch. About 60 Ω means two good terminations in parallel.
  • If one bus is down, unplug branch plugs at the star one at a time and watch the bus voltage and resistance recover. The branch that restores the bus is the shorted one.
  • With a branch plug pulled, the module-side pins should not show a low resistance across H–L or to ground.
  • Per-star values: UNVERIFIED. Because termination is inside the stars, a separated star (trunk C1 unplugged) probably reads about 120 Ω on its own. The manual does not give per-star values.
  • Single-module case (ORC, BSM): the OEM "No Response From ECU" flow checks power and ground before CAN. A dead fuse feed (F85 at 0 V on both sides) puts the ORC fault in steps 2–3, not in CAN.
  • Shared BSM hardware: both BSM sensors' CAN pairs run through the same in-line connectors, I701 and XY4300A (rear-bumper harness). A fault at those connectors could drop both BSM sensors together without any star or bus fault. Their power feed probably passes there too; that is UNVERIFIED and should be checked on the BSM diagram.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The CAN C IP star end views and all C2…C13 branch end views were not fetched.
  • The written OEM location descriptions (as opposed to figures) and the CAN C IP star location figure were not obtained.
  • The "Scan Tool Will Not Communicate With Vehicle" and "Stored Lost Communication DTCs" diagnostic tests were not fetched. They may contain explicit resistance-per-branch steps.

docs.title: Q4. Could one CAN-IHS branch failure cause SRS lamp + BSM + blower + camera failures while the engine runs? Which symptoms do NOT fit a pure CAN failure? Does the HVAC module drive the blower directly (hard-wired) or over CAN?
Takeaway
docs.text:
No. These symptoms are not consistent with a single CAN failure of any kind. The four functions sit on CAN-C, CAN-IHS (Body star), a hard-wired high-current circuit, and LIN plus video respectively. Modules sharing each of those stars still work.

The front blower is driven by wire: - The A/C heater module sends a hard-wired "BLOWER CTRL" signal (circuit C56) to the blower power module. - The power comes from the PDC "Blower Motor Relay" and Fuse 13 (40 A).

So "UI works, speed bars change, motor dead" is a power-path symptom.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• Front blower chain (STRONG INFERENCE from the A/C circuit SVG text) — AC-1, AC-2:
  • PDC side: a "BLOWER MOTOR RELAY" with "FUSE 13" 40 A. The rear blower relay has Fuse 37, 25 A.
  • Supply: relay output circuit C7 (DK BLU) → XY5020A pin 29 → front blower motor power module C1-6 "BLOWER MTR SPLY" → module C2-1 C7 (DK BLU/WHT) → blower motor pin 1.
  • Motor return: motor pin 2 "BLOWER MTR CTRL" (Z134, DK BLU/BRN) → power module C2-2 → module ground C1-5 Z911 → G911A (under front of center console).
  • Control: A/C heater module circuit C56 (DK BLU/BLU) → power module C1-3 "BLOWER CTRL". The label printed beside the C56 pin on the A/C module reads "BLOWER MOTOR SPLY".
  • No network at the power module: WebFetch reported no "CAN", "LIN" or "PWM" text on the power-module sheet.
  • STRONG INFERENCE: the A/C heater module's own network connection is CAN IHS on C1 pins 4/5 (D101/D102 → IHS-IP star C3) — AC-1, CDL-2
  • Modules sharing stars with the failed functions (STRONG INFERENCE):
  • CAN-C IP star: ORC (C2) shares it with the IPC (C5), steering column module (C7), RF Hub (C12) and SGW (C6) — CDL-3
  • CAN-IHS Body star: the BSM sensors (C4/C5) share it with the power liftgate module (C2) and the seat modules — CDL-5
  • IHS-IP star: the A/C module (C3) shares it with the driver and passenger door modules (C2/C10) — CDL-2
  • STRONG INFERENCE: the rear camera's only network connection is BCM LIN CBC 3. It has no CAN pins — CDL-4
  • VERIFIED: the OEM ECU no-response flow load-tests power and ground before checking CAN (see Q3) — No Response From ECU

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• A full CAN-C failure is ruled out. It would take down the IPC, RF Hub, steering column module, PCM/TCM/ABS messaging and SGW→radio reverse status. Keyless start, a working cluster and "radio detects reverse" contradict that.
  • A full CAN-IHS failure is ruled out. It would break:
  • the door-module functions on the IHS-IP star: passenger window from the driver switch, door locks, mirrors;
  • fob-commanded liftgate on the IHS-Body star.

All of these work. Caveat: if the liftgate was tested only with its own hard-wired switch, that does not prove CAN-IHS. - One IHS branch (one 2-pin plug) can drop one module only. Both BSM sensors dropping together fits a shared rear-bumper in-line connector (I701/XY4300A) or a shared power feed better than a bus fault. - Symptoms that do NOT fit any CAN failure: - Front blower motor dead while the UI responds. The motor is powered through Fuse 13 (40 A), the blower relay, circuit C7 and the power module. A CAN loss would leave the module unable to command, but the motor path itself is hard-wired. - Rear camera blue screen. The camera is not a CAN node. The radio switching to the camera view proves the CAN/A-T reverse message arrives. A blue (no-video) screen points to camera power, ground, the video circuit or the camera itself. - ORC dark with F85 at 0 V on both sides. This is a power problem upstream of F85 (the feed to the fuse), not a CAN problem. - Best fit: a common power-source failure that feeds the ORC fuse F85, the blower relay or power module supply, the BSM sensor supply and the camera supply. Engine, charging and CAN infrastructure are intact. - Hypothesis for the power-distribution researcher (UNVERIFIED): the A/C sheet prints "HOT W/ RUN 2 RELAY ENERGIZED" near the blower relays. If F85, the blower relay coil feed and the BSM/camera fuses all hang off one PDC ignition-run relay output or bus, that relay or its feed is the prime suspect. This needs confirmation from the PDC / power-distribution diagrams.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Which PDC relay or bus feeds the blower motor relay coil (and F85) was not resolved from the SVG text.
  • Whether the Uconnect speed bars show the A/C module's echoed status or only the radio's own command was not documented. So the UI working does not by itself prove the A/C heater module is online. A topology scan is needed.
  • The power feeds of the BSM sensors and the rear camera were not extracted. They are not on the data-lines sheets.

docs.title: Q5. Which modules need ORC messages? Do the BSM radars or the camera depend on the ORC?
Takeaway
docs.text: No source I could reach shows the BSM sensors, the rear camera or the HVAC/blower depending on ORC messages. On the network the ORC is a CAN-C node (IP star C2), electrically independent of the CAN-IHS Body star where the BSM sensors sit. An ORC outage should light the SRS lamp, nothing more.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE: ORC network pins are C2 pin 54 "CAN C (+)" (D11) and pin 53 "CAN C (−)" (D12), via XY5020A 11/12 to CAN-C IP star C2 — CDL-3
  • STRONG INFERENCE: the BSM sensors connect only to CAN-IHS Body star plugs C4/C5. The rear camera connects only to BCM LIN CBC 3 — CDL-5, CDL-4
  • VERIFIED: the OEM "No Response From ECU" procedure explicitly excludes load-testing air-bag/restraint circuits. ORC power checks must be done by voltage or approved method only — No Response From ECU

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• Expected DTC pattern with the ORC unpowered: the cluster and other CAN-C nodes log "lost communication with ORC" (generic U0151) and the cluster lights the airbag lamp. Typical FCA behaviour; not confirmed in a 2018 Durango document.
  • BSM, camera and blower: with no documented ORC dependency, their simultaneous failure points to a shared power source, not to the ORC's silence.
  • Scan-tool check that settles it: a topology scan showing ORC, left and right BSM sensors "not responding", while the A/C heater module, BCM, door modules and liftgate respond, confirms a power-feed problem. The next step is voltage checks at each module's fused B+/ignition pins, not a CAN hunt.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• I found no 2018 Durango description of which modules consume ORC broadcast messages (crash status, belt status). The BCM U-code list (DTCs B2119-11 to U1433-24) and the IPC DTC pages were not read.
  • The BSM system's own "Description and Operation" was not fetched; it might list required input messages such as vehicle speed, turn signals or trailer status.

docs.title: Connector-level wiring of the ORC power feeds (F85/F86 → PDC C6 → ORC) — 2018 Dodge Durango (WD) 5.7L AWD
docs.text:
Локальные копии документов

Пути вида docs/sources/... указывают на копии документов в приватном репозитории, на сайте их нет. Пользуйтесь ссылками на оригинальные страницы или указателем источников.

Source basis: everything marked VERIFIED was read from the 2018 Durango factory service information, as reproduced on lemon-manuals.la. The primary manual used is "2018 Durango Citadel, 5.7L Eng VIN T, AWD". The key pages were also pulled from the 2018 "Durango R/T, AWD" manual: the C6 table, ORC C2 table and B212C/B212D test text are byte-identical, and the wiring diagrams use the same image IDs (VA582314, VA586498–501). So the data applies to the subject R/T AWD, VIN 1C4SDJCT3JCXXXXXX. Wiring diagrams are SVG files and were rendered to PNG locally for reading. Pin/colour data come from the HTML tables, not from OCR.

Wire colour codes: 2017–2018 SI uses ISO-style codes (PK = pink, YE = yellow, GN = green, BK = black, BU = blue, DB = dark blue). The diagrams spell them out (PNK/YEL, PNK/GRN, BLK). The 2015 SI uses old Chrysler codes (YL, LG = light green) and AWG gauges.

docs.title: Q1. Which PDC connector is C6? Is it D6630F? What is the 2018 pinout, and does it match the reported 2015 data?
Takeaway
docs.text: VERIFIED. PDC C6 is harness connector D6630F for 2018: LIGHT GRAY, FEMALE, Body harness, part number 7287-8882-40. The 2015 data mostly holds: pin 15 = F929, pin 13 = F945, pin 28 = F931, pin 32 = F925, pin 36 = F948. Only the colour notation changed: 2015 PK/YL and PK/LG are 2018 PK/YE and PK/GN.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED: "Assembly-Power Distribution Center C6 (Standard) Connector End View (D6630F)". Harness-Family Body, Color LIGHT GRAY, Gender FEMALE, Part Number 7287-8882-40, Connector No D6630F. — 2018 PDC C6 end view
  • VERIFIED: 2018 C6 (D6630F) pinout, complete list as published ("Pins not listed are not used"). Columns are pin – circuit – colour – mm² – function. — 2018 PDC C6 end view
  • 1 A400 BG/RD 2.0 FUSED B(+); 2 A949 RD 2.0 FUSED B(+); 3 C15 DB/WH 2.0 REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER CONTROL OUTPUT; 4 C115 DB 0.50 DEFOGGER RELAY CONTROL
  • 7 F949 PK/GN 0.50 FUSED IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT; 8 F942 PK/GN 0.35 FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN-START); 10 K617 BN 0.50 RUN/START RELAY CONTROL
  • 13 F945 PK/GN 0.50 IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT
  • 15 F929 PK/YE 0.50 FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN)
  • 16 L310 BG/WH 0.50 RIGHT HEADLAMP RELAY CONTROL; 17 A130 VT/RD 2.0 FUSED B(+); 19 A918 RD 2.0 FUSED B(+); 21 A904 RD 4.0 FUSED B(+); 24 A111 DG/RD 2.0 FUSED B(+); 26 A932 RD 1.0 FUSED B(+)
  • 28 F931 PK/YE 0.50 FUSED IGNITION RUN CONTROL OUTPUT; 32 F925 PK/YE 0.50 FUSED IGNITION RUN CONTROL OUTPUT; 34 F938 PK/YE 0.50 FUSED IGNITION RUN/START RELAY OUTPUT; 36 F948 PK/GN 0.35 FUSED IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT
  • 38 A401 RD/GN 2.0 FUSED B(+); 39 K90 BU/BG 0.50 STARTER RELAY CONTROL
  • VERIFIED: the 2018 R/T AWD manual's C6 page has an identical pin table and the same part number and colour. — 2018 R/T AWD PDC C6
  • VERIFIED (end-view figure, image GCWD1006494): the cavity numbering callouts are 1 (upper right), 21 (upper left), 22 (lower right) and 42 (lower left). Pins 4 and 5 are called out as an inner small terminal and an outer slot. So numbering alternates between staggered sub-rows; this is a 42-way layout. — C6 end-view image
  • VERIFIED: the PDC layout graphic ("DODGE DURANGO (WD) Underhood Power Distribution Center (PDC)") shows C6 plugged into the rear/top-left area of the PDC. Its fuse table lists F85 "Airbag Module" 10A, F86 "Airbag Module" 10A and F95 "Rear Camera / ParkSense" 10A. — PDC Layout And Connector Identification (image G00621551)

  • STRONG INFERENCE: 2017 R/T AWD C6 is identical to 2018 (PK/YE, PK/GN, metric sizes). — 2017 R/T AWD PDC C6
  • VERIFIED (what the other cited pins feed, from Power Distribution diagram 1 of 4, VA586498):
  • C6-28 (F931) is the load side of fuse 103 10A. It is jumpered to C7-8, which goes to the Rear Blower Motor Relay coil (85).
  • C6-32 (F925) is the load side of fuse 101 15A. Path: XY5020A-7 → S2443 → in-car temperature sensor and humidity sensor.
  • C6-34 is the load side of fuse 100 10A. Path: XY6020A-33 → XY8200A-8 → SP2589 → Active Damping Control Module C2-14/47.
  • C6-36 (F948) is the load side of fuse 99 10A on the Run/Start relay (diagram 3 of 4, VA586500). Path: S2448 → Park Assist, A/C heater module C1-1, Forward Facing Camera, Rear A/C heater control module, Adaptive Cruise.

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• The connector identification needs no correction for 2018: C6 = D6630F, same part number since 2015, same circuit codes. Only the colour notation changed (PK/LG → PK/GN; PK/YL → PK/YE) and gauges moved from AWG to mm² (22 ga ≈ 0.35–0.5 mm²).
  • In the C6 table only F929 (pin 15) is described as "FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN)". Pins 28 and 32 are "FUSED IGNITION RUN CONTROL OUTPUT". All three PK/YE circuits come off the same Run 2 relay output bus (see Q2).

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The exact physical cavity location of pin 15 within the staggered 42-way face was not resolved. The figure only labels pins 1, 4, 5, 21, 22 and 42; use the numbers moulded on the connector. The table also does not state whether the end view shows the terminal side or the wire side.
  • The PDC fuse/relay table graphic is low-resolution (853×635 px). The fuse numbers are legible; the relay "Alternate" codes are not reliably legible.

docs.title: Q2. Is C6 pin 15 the output (load side) of F85 or an input? What feeds F85?
Takeaway
docs.text: VERIFIED. C6-15 is the load (output) side of fuse 85. Inside the PDC, F85's supply side is fed by the RUN 2 relay (contact 87). F85 output → C6-15 → PK/YE F929 → ORC C2-104. The same Run 2 relay output also feeds fuses 40, 103, 101 and 100. The Run 2 relay coil (85) is fed from the Run 1 relay output bus, which also feeds F95. The coil return (86) shares the PDC ground bus with the Run 1 relay coil: PDC C1-12 → S2547 → G909A.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED (SRS diagram 1 of 3, VA582314): the PDC block shows "FUSE 85 10A" labelled "HOT W/ RUN 2 RELAY ENERGIZED" and "FUSE 86 10A" labelled "HOT W/ RUN/START RELAY ENERGIZED". Fuse 85's lower terminal exits at C6 pin 15 → PNK/YEL → ORC pin 104 "FUSED IGN SW OUTPUT (RUN)" F929. Fuse 86 exits at C6 pin 13 → PNK/GRN → ORC pin 103 "IGN RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT" F945. — Supplemental Restraints diagrams, image VA582314
  • VERIFIED (Power Distribution diagram 1 of 4, VA586498): RUN 2 RELAY contact 30 connects to the PDC B+ bus. Contact 87 drives a bus feeding FUSE 40 10A, FUSE 103 10A, FUSE 85 10A, FUSE 101 15A and FUSE 100 10A.
  • Fuse 85 → pin 15 → PNK/YEL → "104 C2 OCCUPANT RESTRAINT CONTROLLER MODULE". The dashed connector line joins pins 15, 32 and 34, and the group is labelled C6.
  • No in-line connector or splice is drawn on this run.
  • Source: Power Distribution diagrams, image VA586498; local crop renders/2018_Durango_PD1of4_crop_RUN2_relay_F85_C6pin15.png
  • VERIFIED (same diagram): RUN 1 RELAY contact 87 drives fuses 95 (10A), 96 (10A), 98 (20A) and 97 (20A). The same Run 1 output line also connects to the RUN 2 RELAY coil terminal 85 and the (front) BLOWER MOTOR RELAY coil terminal 85.
  • Run 1 relay coil 85 → C7-12 → BRN/ORG → Body Control Module C5-36.
  • Run 1 and Run 2 relay coil terminals 86 join a common line inside the PDC.
  • Source: VA586498; local crop renders/2018_Durango_PD1of4_crop_RUN1_RUN2_relay_coils.png
  • VERIFIED (Ground Distribution diagram 1 of 4, VA586554): inside the PDC, coil terminals of several relays tie to one bus that exits PDC C1 pin 12 → BLK → S2547 (front fascia, front end module harness) → XY8120A-6 → G909A (right rear of engine compartment). The relays are Run 1 (86), Run 2 (86), Run/Accessory 1 and 2, Run/Start (86), Horn, HID, Wiper and Rear window defogger. — Ground Distribution diagrams, image VA586554
  • VERIFIED (same Power Distribution 1 of 4): fuse 95 → C7-13 → PNK/YEL → S2442 ("right front door sill, w/ blind spot").
  • Branch XY4000A-12 → I701-J → S04A F923 → right and left rear blind spot sensors (pin 5).
  • Branch XY2120A-6 → I6742A-1 → RED → rear video camera pin 3.
  • Source: VA586498; local crop renders/2018_Durango_PD1of4_crop_RUN1_relay_F95_BSM_camera.png
  • VERIFIED (A/C diagram 1 of 4, VA585297):
  • Fuse 103 and Fuse 101 are both labelled "HOT W/ RUN 2 RELAY ENERGIZED".
  • Fuse 103 → C6-28 → C7-8 → REAR BLOWER MOTOR RELAY coil 85. Its coil 86 → C7-4 → S2505 → G919A.
  • The (front) BLOWER MOTOR RELAY coil 86 → C7-16 → S2505 → G919A.
  • Front blower relay contact 87 → FUSE 13 40A → C7-21 → DK BLU (to the blower power module, continued off-page).
  • Source: Air Conditioning diagrams, image VA585297
  • UNVERIFIED (low-resolution table in the PDC layout graphic): relay list reads approximately K08 "Run / Start", K12 "Run 2", K13 "Blower Motor - Rear", K15 "Run 1", K16 "Blower Motor". — PDC layout image G00621551
  • STRONG INFERENCE: the 2015 SRS diagram shows the same arrangement: "HOT W/ RUN 2" fuse 85 10A → C6-15 → ORC 104 PNK/YEL F929, and fuse 86 → C6-13 → ORC 103 PNK/LT GRN F945. — 2015 R/T AWD Supplemental Restraints
  • SECONDARY: an owner's-manual-derived fuse list gives F85 and F86 both "Airbag Module" 10A and F95 "Rear Camera / ParkSense" 10A. The same list gives F100 as 15A and F103 as 20A, which conflicts with the factory graphic and diagram (10A). — startmycar 2018 Durango fuse box

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE about the measurement. F85 reads 0 V on both test points in RUN while F86 and F95 are normal. So the fault is upstream of the fuse, i.e. the Run 2 relay output bus. An open F85 element would still leave 12 V on the supply-side test point.
  • STRONG INFERENCE: the supply chain that should energise Run 2 appears healthy:
  • Coil feed (Run 1 output bus) is live, since F95 is live.
  • Coil return is shared with the Run 1 coil (C1-12 → G909A), and Run 1 works.
  • Contact 30 is on the PDC B+ bus.
  • Prime suspects are therefore the Run 2 relay itself, its socket terminals, or an internal PDC bus or trace break.
  • Quick non-SRS cross-check: all fuses on the Run 2 output (F40, F103, F101, F100) should also read 0 V in RUN. Seeing 0 V on them confirms a dead Run 2 output bus without touching any ORC/SRS connector.
  • Consequence to confirm with other researchers: F103 (Run 2) feeds the rear blower motor relay coil, so the rear blower should also be dead.
  • Out of scope, but flagged for the synthesis writer: per the 2018 diagrams, BSM sensors and the rear camera are on F95 (Run 1), not F85. The front blower relay coil is on the Run 1 bus. Their failure therefore is not explained by a loss of F85 itself. It must come from something else, e.g. a different feed, a CAN/module dependency, or a shared ground such as S2505/G919A for the blower relay coils. Not investigated here.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The internal PDC bus structure cannot be serviced or probed from the diagrams; they only show logical connections. Run 2 relay socket cavity numbering was not found.
  • The front blower motor power module feed and ground (A/C diagram 2 of 4) were not reviewed. The renders saved are pages 1 of 4 only.

docs.title: Q3. ORC connectors: connector numbers, pins for Ignition RUN (F929) and RUN/START (F945), grounds, CAN, colours; in-line connectors or splices between PDC and ORC
Takeaway
docs.text:
VERIFIED. The ORC has three harness connectors. C1 = D3834A (IP harness, squibs only), C2 = D3834B (Body harness: power, ground, CAN and all sensors) and C3 = D3834C (side impact sensor 2). Power and ground are on C2: - pin 104 = F929 PK/YE 0.50 "FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN)" (from F85) - pin 103 = F945 PK/GN 0.50 "IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT" (from F86) - pin 101 = Z913 BK 0.50 GROUND → G913A (under rear of center console) - CAN C on pins 53 (D12 YE, −) and 54 (D11 YE/DB, +)

No in-line connector or splice is drawn on F929 or F945 between PDC C6 and ORC C2.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED: ORC C2 (D3834B) is YELLOW, FEMALE, Body harness, PN F577100. Pins: 53 D12 YE 0.35 CAN C (−); 54 D11 YE/DB 0.35 CAN C (+); 101 Z913 BK 0.50 GROUND; 103 F945 PK/GN 0.50 IGNITION RUN/START CONTROL OUTPUT; 104 F929 PK/YE 0.50 FUSED IGNITION SWITCH OUTPUT (RUN). The remaining pins are sensors, squibs and tensioners: 55–99 including R41 at 99 "AIRBAG DEPLOYMENT SIGNAL". — 2018 ORC C2 end view
  • VERIFIED: ORC C1 (D3834A) is YELLOW, FEMALE, IP harness, PN F067100. Its pins are only front squib lines: 6/7 driver knee blocker; 11/12 driver squib 2; 13/14 passenger squib 2; 16/17 passenger squib 1; 18/19 driver squib 1. No power or ground. — 2018 ORC C1 end view
  • VERIFIED: ORC C3 (D3834C) is YELLOW, FEMALE, Body harness, PN F477100. Pins 1–4: right/left side impact sensor 2 signal and ground (R17–R20). — 2018 ORC C3 end view
  • VERIFIED (SRS diagram 1 of 3): the ORC is labelled "(UNDER REAR OF CENTER CONSOLE)" with connector label C2 on pins 53–104.
  • 104 PNK/YEL F929 runs to PDC C6-15.
  • 103 PNK/GRN F945 runs to PDC C6-13.
  • 101 BLK Z913 → ground G913A (UNDER REAR OF CENTER CONSOLE).
  • 53/54 D12/D11 → "COMPUTER DATA LINES SYSTEM".
  • No in-line connector symbol appears on the F929 or F945 lines. The only in-line connector in that area is XY5010A-28, on the R41 airbag deployment signal to the radio.
  • Source: VA582314
  • VERIFIED (Ground Distribution 3 of 4, VA586556): "OCCUPANT RESTRAINT CONTROLLER MODULE 101 C2 → BLK → G913A (UNDER REAR OF CENTER CONSOLE)". This is a dedicated eyelet, not shared with other modules on that page. — VA586556
  • VERIFIED (R/T AWD cross-check): the 2018 R/T AWD ORC C2 pin table is identical. — 2018 R/T AWD ORC C2
  • VERIFIED: ORC Operation text says the ORC "receives battery current through two circuits": a fused ignition output (run) circuit and a fused ignition output (run-start) circuit, each through a PDC fuse. It also says ground comes through "a take out of the instrument panel wire harness" secured by a ground screw. That text conflicts with the end-view table, where Z913 is on C2, the Body-harness-family connector. — ORC Operation
  • VERIFIED: the ORC is mounted on the floor-panel transmission tunnel under the center console. The IP and body harness connectors attach on the rearward-facing side with lever locks; disconnect the smaller connector first. — ORC Removal
  • STRONG INFERENCE (2015/2017): ORC C2 pins 101/103/104 are unchanged. 2015 uses Z913 BK, F945 PK/LG 22 ga and F929 PK/YL 22 ga. — 2015 R/T AWD ORC C2

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE: the ORC has no constant-B+ input per the 2018 diagram and pin tables. Only the two ignition feeds (C2-104 via F85/Run 2 and C2-103 via F86/Run-Start) plus ground C2-101 are present. The B212C/D "Theory of Operation" text says "battery and ignition feed", which looks like generic template text.
  • STRONG INFERENCE: PDC C6 and ORC C2 are both "Body" harness family, and no in-line connector is drawn. F929 is therefore most likely one continuous wire in the body harness from the PDC (right side of the engine compartment) to the center-console tunnel. An open in this wire is unlikely to explain the observation, because F85 is dead on its supply side.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Exact physical cavity positions of pins 101/103/104 on the D3834B face were not transcribed. The figure is saved as images/2018_Durango_ORC_C2_D3834B_end_view__GCWD1006287.png.
  • Harness routing and pass-through between the engine compartment and the cabin for F929 was not found in the pages reviewed.

docs.title: Q4. Factory diagnostic procedures for B212D-13 (Ignition RUN Only Input – Circuit Open) and B212C-13 (Ignition RUN/START Input – Circuit Open)
Takeaway
docs.text:
VERIFIED, with caveats. Both DTCs set when ignition voltage on the respective input is missing or below 6 V for more than 15 s while the battery circuit maintains system voltage. Both name the correct 2018 fuses in "Possible Causes": F85 for B212D (F929) and F86 for B212C (F945). However, the "Diagnostic Test" step text is templated from another platform: - it references "fuse F6" (B212D) and "fuse F24" (B212C), - it says "ORC module C1 body harness connector", - it says "Rear Power Distribution Center".

Use 2018 mapping instead: F85/F86, PDC C6-15/13, ORC C2-104/103.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED — B212D-13 Set Condition: "sets when the ORC fails to detect ignition voltage or if there is less than 6 volts on the ignition voltage supply circuit for more than 15 seconds while the battery circuit maintains system operating voltage". It transitions to stored after 5 s of normal voltage. — B212D-13 Set Condition
  • VERIFIED — When monitored (both DTCs): at power-up initialisation and every 100 ms during the ignition cycle. — B212D-13 When Monitored
  • VERIFIED — B212D-13 Possible Causes: Active PDC trouble codes; (F929) RUN RELAY CIRCUIT OPEN; POWER DISTRIBUTION CENTER FUSE F85 OPEN; (F929) FUSED RUN RELAY OUTPUT CIRCUIT OPEN OR SHORTED TO GROUND; ORC. The page also says to perform Pre-Diagnostic Troubleshooting first. — B212D-13 Possible Causes
  • VERIFIED — B212D-13 Diagnostic Test steps (paraphrased; full text saved):
  • Notes: use only a DMM that applies no more than 20 mA to a circuit. Probe ORC harness cavities only with Miller test lead 10159-6 (kit 10159) or equivalent. Battery must be fully charged.
  • (1) Ignition on; scan for active B212D-13. If it is not active, run the Intermittent Test.
  • (2) Ignition off, battery disconnected, wait 2 min; remove and inspect the "Airbag Run Circuit Fuse No. F6" [2018 = F85]. If open, go to 3; if OK, go to 6.
  • (3) Measure resistance F929 from the fuse terminal to ground; threshold 100 Ω.
  • (4) Disconnect the ORC connectors; measure F929 resistance at the "ORC module C1 body harness connector" [2018 = C2-104] to ground; threshold 100 Ω.
  • (5) Ignition on; measure voltage at the fuse supply side. Above 6.0 V → go to 6; otherwise "Repair the open (F929) Run Relay Output circuit".
  • (6) Reinstall the fuse, disconnect the ORC, follow the ignition-on/battery-reconnect warning. Measure F929 voltage at the ORC harness connector to ground. Above 6.0 V → replace ORC; otherwise repair the open F929 circuit.
  • Finally run the Restraints System Verification Test.
  • Source: B212D-13 Diagnostic Test
  • VERIFIED — B212C-13 Possible Causes: Active PDC trouble codes; (F945) RUN/START RELAY CIRCUIT OPEN; POWER DISTRIBUTION CENTER FUSE F86 OPEN; (F945) FUSED RUN/START RELAY OUTPUT CIRCUIT OPEN OR SHORTED TO GROUND; ORC. — B212C-13 Possible Causes
  • VERIFIED — B212C-13 Diagnostic Test steps (paraphrased):
  • (1) Read active DTC.
  • (2) Inspect "fuse F24" [2018 = F86].
  • (3) Resistance F945 from fuse output side to ground below 100 Ω?
  • (4) With both ORC connectors disconnected, F945 resistance at the "ORC module C1 body harness connector" [2018 = C2-103] to ground.
  • (5) Ignition on; voltage at the fuse supply side above 6.0 V?
  • (6) Fuse reinstalled, ORC disconnected, ignition on per warning; voltage at the ORC harness connector above 6.0 V?
  • (7) Reconnect; if B212C-13 is still active, replace the ORC.
  • Then run the Verification Test.
  • Source: B212C-13 Diagnostic Test
  • VERIFIED — The R/T AWD copies of both Diagnostic Test pages are identical, including the F6/F24 references. — R/T B212D-13 Diagnostic Test
  • VERIFIED — The B212D-16 (Voltage Below Threshold) Set Condition text says "less than 16 volts", which looks like a typo for 6 V. Its Possible Causes list "ACTIVE POWER DISTRIBUTION CENTER RUN RELAY TROUBLE CODES" and F85 open. — B212D-16 Set Condition
  • VERIFIED — Verification Test:
  • Reconnect everything except the battery, then follow the ignition-on warning.
  • Erase stored DTCs in all airbag modules, perform module reset, wait 1 min and read active then stored codes.
  • If the battery was disconnected, perform the Battery Reconnection procedure.
  • If the ORC was replaced, perform ORC initialisation, and ESC re-initialisation may be needed.
  • Source: Restraints System Verification Test

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• STRONG INFERENCE: the observed state (F85 0 V on both test points, F86 normal) should produce an active B212D-13 and no B212C. In the test flow, step 5 ("voltage at fuse supply side > 6 V?") would answer No, pointing to "open (F929) Run Relay Output circuit". On this platform the supply side of F85 is the PDC-internal Run 2 relay output bus, not a harness wire, so the actual repair target is the Run 2 relay or the PDC (see Q2).
  • UNVERIFIED (logic reading of the published text): B212D-13 step 4 says "below 100 Ω → Go To 5; not below → replace ORC". That looks inverted or garbled relative to the B212D-16 version, where "below 100 Ω → repair short to ground". Any low-resistance-to-ground finding on F929 with the ORC unplugged should be treated as a harness short. The page text should not be followed literally there.
  • No B212D test step needs probing at the ORC connector until the PDC side is restored. Fuse-cavity voltage checks at the PDC are non-SRS measurements. Checking F40/F103/F101/F100 confirms the bus without touching the SRS.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Intermittent Test and Pre-Diagnostic pages were saved but not summarised in detail: generic six-step checklist; address voltage/communication DTCs first.
  • No 2018-specific TSB about the Run 2 relay or the PDC was found. A TSB search was not performed in this task.
  • Web search found no independent 2018 Durango case reports tying B212D to F85 or Run 2. The search results were generic or for older TIPM platforms; obdadvisor B212D is generic Chrysler.

docs.title: Q5. ORC power and grounds diagram, and SRS service precautions
Takeaway
docs.text: VERIFIED. The 2018 SI has no standalone "ORC Power & Grounds" diagram. Power and ground appear on Supplemental Restraints diagram 1 of 3 (VA582314) and in Ground Distribution 3 of 4 (G913A). Mandatory precautions: - Disconnect and isolate the negative battery cable; the IBS connector comes off first. - Wait 2 minutes for the ORC capacitor to discharge. - Use a DMM that applies no more than 20 mA, and only test lead 10159-6 at ORC connectors. - Never drop the ORC; a dropped unit must be replaced. - Repair SRS wiring only with Mopar kits. - Squib circuits on ORC C1 and C2 R-circuits must never be probed or powered.

docs.title: Cited Findings
docs.text:
• VERIFIED: SRS Warning page:
  • Disable the SRS before any ORC diagnosis or service: disconnect and isolate the battery negative cable, then wait two minutes for the system capacitor to discharge. This is "the only sure way to disable the SRS".
  • An ORC with a rollover sensor rolled while powered will deploy the side curtains.
  • Never repair SRS circuits for which there is no Mopar wiring repair kit.
  • For welding, disconnect both battery cables and ground the positive cable to discharge the ORC capacitor.
  • Source: Restraints System Warning
  • VERIFIED: ORC Removal: disconnect the IBS connector first, then the negative cable, and wait two minutes. Never strike or drop the ORC; a dropped ORC "must be scrapped and replaced". — ORC Removal
  • VERIFIED: B212C and B212D tests both state the 20 mA DMM limit and test lead 10159-6. They give two ignition-on warnings:
  • Key ignition: turn the ignition on, then reconnect the battery and wait 2 min.
  • Keyless ignition: disconnect the battery and wait 2 min; remove the ORC fuses; reconnect the battery and wait 2 min; cycle ignition On; reinstall the ORC fuses; wait 2 min.
  • Source: B212C-13 Diagnostic Test
  • VERIFIED: the ORC contains an energy-storage capacitor that can deploy SRS components for up to one second after a battery disconnect or failure. — ORC Operation
  • VERIFIED: the ORC houses a microcontroller, electronic impact sensor, safing sensor, rollover sensor and energy-storage capacitor. The label arrow must point forward. — ORC Description
  • VERIFIED: SRS Diagnosis & Testing: hard-wired SRS circuits may be diagnosed conventionally, but SRS diagnosis requires a scan tool and may need the SRS Load Tool with jumpers and adapters. — SRS Diagnosis and Testing

docs.title: Inferences
docs.text:
• Practical safe-diagnosis order consistent with the SI:
  • Diagnose F85's dead supply entirely at the PDC: fuse cavities, Run 2 relay, and the other Run 2 fuses F40/F103/F101/F100.
  • Only after F85 is live, check the C6-15 → ORC C2-104 continuity or voltage per B212D steps. Follow the battery-disconnect, 2-minute and test-lead rules.
  • Never back-probe the ORC C1 squib pins or the C2 R-circuits.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Inaccessible:
